presets.name: Organ chorale, slow
presets.desc: Classic two-rotor cabinet at slow speed: gentle Doppler swirl, ready to ramp to fast by footswitch

refs.why: organ-trio tone: tonewheel organ through a spinning cabinet

presets.notes: Stock 122 inertia (horn 0.16/0.32 s, drum 4.1/1.4 s): put speed on a footswitch, the slow-to-fast ramp is the sound

presets.name: Organ fast tremolo
presets.desc: Both rotors at full speed: the shimmering, warbling organ tone for climaxes and fills

refs.why: tonewheel organ riff with a spinning cabinet

presets.notes: Slight horn bias (balance 55) and depth 65 bring the fast warble forward in a band mix

presets.name: Overdriven rock organ
presets.desc: Close-miked cabinet with its tube preamp pushed: growling, gritty organ for hard rock

refs.why: Jon Lord's distorted, aggressive rock organ
Gregg Allman's gritty organ through a spinning cabinet

presets.notes: The crate's organ-growl start: 147 with drive 60+ before the crossover, mic close for more AM and bite

presets.name: Lazy ballad spin-up
presets.desc: Slow cabinet with long, drawn-out speed changes: the swell to fast takes several bars

refs.why: slow, churchy organ swirl carrying the ballad

presets.notes: Ramp 220 % stretches all four time constants: the drum takes ~9 s to reach full speed

presets.name: Gospel quick-switch shout
presets.desc: Punchy cabinet with snappy speed changes and some preamp grit, for stabbing between slow and fast
presets.notes: Ramp 55 % makes the switch answer quickly for church-style speed stabs

presets.name: Guitar drum-rotor warble
presets.desc: Drum-only guitar rotary at fast speed: a thick, liquid warble on clean blues chords

refs.why: rotating-speaker cabinet on the clean rhythm part

presets.notes: The crate's guitar-Leslie start; Vibratone = one rotor, full range, so balance does not matter

presets.name: Warbly grunge verse
presets.desc: Drum-rotor cabinet driven by a cranked amp: a woozy, slightly gritty warble on arpeggios

refs.why: verse guitar through a Leslie 16 powered by a Marshall

presets.notes: Drum fast 5 Hz, a little under stock, gives the lazier warble; more wobble for the drifting feel

presets.name: Wide clean-chord swirl
presets.desc: Far, widely spaced mics at slow speed: lush stereo movement on clean guitar chords

refs.why: Harrison's guitar fed through a rotating speaker

presets.notes: The crate's wide-chords start: mic 85 adds reflections, spacing 85 opens the stereo

presets.name: Subtle rotor thickener
presets.desc: Slow rotary blended under the dry signal: light movement and width that keeps the attack
presets.notes: Mix 40 / depth 40: the dry stays dominant, the cabinet only adds air and motion

presets.name: Spinning-speaker vocal
presets.desc: A voice through a fast rotating cabinet: swirling, distant, otherworldly lead vocal

refs.why: Lennon's vocal re-recorded through a Leslie cabinet
refs.source: Geoff Emerick, Here, There and Everywhere, 2006

presets.notes: Horn-heavy balance keeps the voice intelligible; low drive avoids grit on sibilants

presets.name: Airy rear-cab electric piano
presets.desc: Slow rotary heard from behind the open cabinet: soft, airy swirl on electric piano
presets.notes: Rear cab and far mics trade bite for air, which suits tine pianos better than the front 122

presets.name: Brake to a stop
presets.desc: Rotors coast to a halt with the horn parked at the mic: a dramatic stop to a static, boxy tone
presets.notes: Recall it from a moving speed: brake 60 coasts, stop angle 0° parks the horn facing the mic (brightest)

presets.name: Bass rotor with solid lows
presets.desc: Slow drum rotor on bass, sub-bass kept mono and still, half blended with the dry
presets.notes: Bass keep at its 200 Hz maximum plus mix 60 keep the fundamental steady; only the upper harmonics swirl

presets.name: Mono-safe rotary
presets.desc: Slow/fast cabinet with coincident mics: exactly mono, no hollow sum on a mono PA
presets.notes: Spacing 0 = L equals R: the AM and Doppler survive mono summing on small venue PAs
